Expiration dates might seem insignificant at first, but they ultimately serve as a bellwether for the quality and safety of perishable goods. Over time, even seemingly robust items will inevitably deteriorate--whether due to natural degradation or improper storage. Thus, properly identifying and managing expiration dates represents a critical checkpoint in the sustainability of food supplies. 

For consumers, understanding expiration dates should be a matter of basic caution; otherwise, one risks either consuming spoiled food or wasting resources. In general, most products come labeled with some sort of date code which indicates their freshness and/or shelf life. It is important to recognize these codes and pay attention to them, since different types of expired goods present different kinds of hazards (e.g., health dangers from spoiled food, environmental threats from leaking chemicals).
